verdict: AppLovin turned $1.92B of revenue (+53%) into $1.27B of net profit — a 66% margin — as its AXON ad platform kept compounding.

segments.name: Advertising platform
segments.note: Ads placed through AppLovin's AXON platform — advertisers pay to reach users inside other companies' apps, and AXON's AI decides which ads to show.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building and improving the AXON ad platform — more than doubled year over year (+127%) as AppLovin pours money into AI-driven ad targeting.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to advertisers and app publishers — up 35% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — down 27% YoY as AppLovin streamlined after selling its apps business.

otherDetail: Other income of $62M (mostly investment and foreign-exchange gains), partly offset by $51M of interest expense on AppLovin's debt.

takeaways.title: Growth is barely slowing
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 53% year over year to $1.92B — and AppLovin guided the next quarter to about $2.07B, so the ad engine was still accelerating into the fall.

takeaways.title: Two of every three dollars became profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $1,267M — a 66% margin. The whole running-cost bill (R&D, sales, admin) was just $204M against $1,924M of revenue.

takeaways.title: A cash machine
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $863M in a single quarter, and AppLovin spent $551M of it buying back its own shares.

footerNote: AppLovin reports as a single segment. Its former apps business was sold in 2025 and appears as discontinued operations in earlier periods; there were none this quarter.
